A 95 mm aluminium plate on a shaker (Modal Shop K2004E01) was driven in the vertical axis by a single square-wave pulse of about 0.0005 s (broadband, described as biologically relevant up to 1000 Hz); a laser Doppler vibrometer (Polytec VibroOne) measured vertical velocity at 50 pre-determined points on the body, three pulses per point, averaged. FRF = frequency response function (body motion relative to the plate input). This is a mechanical transfer measurement on the animal's body, not a neural threshold or a behavioural response. Vertical axis only; no horizontal or rotational motion measured. Main already holds a row from this paper's abstract (legs damp body resonance, raising signal-to-noise at the leg tips); this record is a different, frequency-specific Results finding. Plate 95 mm diameter, 4 mm thick; 25.6 kHz sampling.
